name: Rush
author: Erin Carter
description: A rank of cattail rushes silhouetted against a glowing dusk sky along a waterline, with a low sun on the horizon — and below, a prominent rippling reflection of the whole scene: the reflected dusk sky, a shimmering sun-glitter column, and the dark mirrored reeds wavering on the water. A gust front crosses the bed stem by stem, each rush bowing and overshooting with glow gathering on its downwind edge, the reflection echoing every gesture a beat late.

params.label: Sway speed
params.effect: Pace of the reeds' gentle continuous sway — low is a barely-there drift, high a livelier breeze.

params.label: Sway amount
params.effect: How far the rushes lean as they drift — 0 holds them dead still, high leans them well over.

params.label: Reed spacing
params.effect: CSS-pixel spacing between rushes along the waterline, from a dense reed bed to a sparse stand.

params.label: Reflection
params.effect: Strength of the mirrored reeds in the water, from just the reflected sky to deep vivid reed reflections.

params.label: Variation
params.effect: Spread of per-stem height and sway timing — 0 lines the rushes up as an even rank of identical reeds, 1 gives the full natural scatter of a wild reed bed.

params.label: Reed height
params.effect: Overall height of the rushes from the waterline — low leaves a short marsh fringe, high stands tall reeds against the sky.

params.label: Sun position
params.effect: Where the low dusk sun sits along the horizon — its glow and the shimmering glitter column below it slide with it.

params.label: Ripple
params.effect: Strength of the water's ripple and shimmer — 0 stills it to a clean mirror, high churns the reflection into broken wavering bands.

params.label: Sky glow
params.effect: Brightness of the dusk sky and its reflection — low sinks the scene toward night, high flares a vivid sunset glow.

params.label: Hills
params.effect: Height of the rolling far-shore hills behind the reeds (and their reflection) — 0 is a flat open horizon, high raises distant hills to sell the lake's depth.
